newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end sharply lower, pork bellies higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end sharply lower, pork bellies higher.

text.p: CME hog futures remained under pressure at the close from a combination of profit taking, fund selling and long liquidation prompted by further weakness in cash markets, traders said.
Pork bellies rallied to end higher on short covering and ideas cash product has bottomed, traders said.
Hogs closed 0.925 cent per lb lower to unchanged with April off most at 69.175 cents. Pork bellies finished 1.150 to 0.050 higher with May up 0.625 at 76.500 cents.
Initial gains in hogs sparked by lower grain price expectations failed to hold and hog futures sank on concerns over a weak tone to pork products and cash hogs, traders said.
The latest CME lean hog index fell $1.10 to $68.18 per cwt. Floor traders also cited calls for $0.50 per cwt lower cash hog markets Wednesday.
"Product is still under pressure," said Julia Bussie, livestock analyst for AG Edwards.

Sell stops added to early losses and only light short covering lifted futures from day's lows late. Mostly lower quotes for cash pork at noon and expectations for lower cash hog prices Wednesday weighed on futures, they said.
Futures had a premium built in, expecting higher cash prices by this time of year. But recent weak pork prices and only tepid packer demand for hogs kept cash markets pressured.

"I think the trade is getting suspect, as we are getting close here to April, that there's too much premium in there and maybe we got too much in June and July also," said Don Roose, President of U.S. Commodities Inc.

Goldman Sachs rolling out of April hogs weighed on that month and R.J. O'Brien sold April while FIMAT Futures USA sold June, traders said. Cargill Investor Services bought June. In hog options, there was general buying of April 74 and lower puts, pit sources said.

Pork bellies rallied again late on renewed short covering prompted by firmer cash ideas which offset the outlook for increased storings. USDA quoted cash bellies steady at noon and prices could be higher by Wednesday, traders said.
"We saw expanded interest from user types," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp.

Technically the market also looked oversold after a nine- cent break last week. March fell to a major trend line on the charts Monday and held early despite heavy deliveries. Those deliveries may have gone to strong hands, traders added.

After the close, the CME reported a net in-movement at warehouses outside Chicago last week of 1.833 million lbs, above analyst and trader expectations of an in-movement of 1.0 million to 1.5 million lbs.
